name: Line / stroke language
controls: Whether elements have outlines, how heavy and consistent those lines are, what tool they imitate, and how lines are drawn in motion.
question: How should lines and outlines be drawn, if at all?
notes: Options mix three independent axes: weight (hairline, thin, medium, heavy, chunky), consistency (uniform, variable width, monoline), and tool or character (rough, hand-drawn, technical, marker, ink, double-line, offset-line), plus one motion option (animated draw-on). Pick one weight and optionally one character. All px weights are for a 1920x1080 frame; scale proportionally for 4K or vertical formats, and use vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke so scaling SVGs never changes weight. Interaction with illustration: stroke weight should match illustration scale; heavy outlines flatten illustration into cartoon or sticker styles, no outlines push it toward flat-vector or 3D; variable-width strokes read as drawn by hand or brush. Interaction with UI: real interfaces use 1px hairline borders and 1.5-2px icon strokes, so a video that enlarges UI must decide whether strokes scale with it (true to product) or stay thin (true to screen crispness). Icon strokes, UI borders, illustration outlines and chart lines should share one stroke logic, or at most two deliberate weights. 'Monoline' overlaps with uniform; here monoline means a single continuous-weight line used as the whole drawing style.

options.what: Forms are defined only by fills and value contrast, never by lines.
options.looks: Flat or shaded color shapes meeting edge to edge; separation comes from color and shadow.
options.motion: Shape morphs, fills sweeping, masks; no draw-on.
options.use: Flat-vector illustration, 3D-leaning styles, premium UI films, color-field graphics.
options.vs: Hairline strokes are nearly invisible but still present; no outlines relies entirely on fill contrast.
options.prompt: Use no strokes anywhere: separate every shape by fill color and value contrast (at least 15% lightness difference between adjacent shapes) or soft shadow. UI cards have no borders; icons are filled.

options.what: The thinnest visible line, about 1px at 1080p.
options.looks: Delicate borders, fine dividers, subtle grid lines, precise diagrams.
options.motion: Lines extend and retract, grid lines drawing across the frame, slow reveals so lines survive compression.
options.use: Premium UI, editorial layouts, luxury brands, technical overlays.
options.vs: Thin (1.5-2px) is clearly visible on video; hairlines can flicker or vanish when compressed or moving fast.
options.prompt: Use 1px strokes (1.5px if the line moves) in 10-20% contrast against the background for borders, dividers and grid lines. Keep motion on hairlines slow (500ms+) and on whole pixels to avoid shimmering; never animate a hairline's thickness.

options.what: Light, clearly visible lines, about 1.5-2px at 1080p.
options.looks: Standard UI icon weight, light illustration outlines, clean diagrams.
options.use: SaaS icons, line illustrations, flowcharts, UI borders scaled up.
options.vs: Hairline is more delicate; medium (3-4px) starts to feel graphic.
options.prompt: Use 2px strokes (1080p) with round caps and joins for icons, connectors and illustration outlines; one weight throughout. Draw on with stroke-dashoffset over 400-600ms, ease power1.inOut.

options.looks: Confident outlines, readable at small sizes, friendly illustration weight.
options.motion: Draw-ons, wiggle and boil, clear connector animations.
options.use: Explainers, friendly illustration, icons displayed large, diagrams for social video.
options.vs: Thin reads delicate; heavy (6-8px) reads bold and cartoonish.
options.prompt: Use 3-4px strokes (1080p) with round caps and joins for all outlines and icons, dark neutral or brand-dark color. Keep one weight; details inside shapes use 2px max.

options.looks: Strong cartoon-like outlines, graphic punch, high contrast.
options.motion: Bold draw-ons, pops, squash and stretch where outlines deform with shapes.
options.use: Playful brands, stickers, comics-influenced styles, kids and gaming.
options.vs: Chunky (10px+) is even heavier and nearly graphic-block; medium is friendlier and lighter.
options.prompt: Outline every shape with 6-8px strokes (1080p) in near-black (#111) with round joins; fills are flat and saturated. Outlines scale and deform with their shapes during squash and stretch.

options.what: Very thick outlines, 10px and above at 1080p, where the line becomes a graphic element in itself.
options.looks: Fat outlines, simplified forms, sticker or toy-like appearance, neo-brutalist UI borders.
options.motion: Blocky pops, hard offsets, stamp-like entrances.
options.use: Neo-brutalist brands, youth and gaming, sticker styles, loud social ads.
options.vs: Heavy is bold but still an outline; chunky dominates the shape and usually pairs with hard offset shadows.
options.prompt: Use 10-14px black outlines (1080p) on shapes, cards and buttons, square or round joins consistently, paired with flat saturated fills and hard offset shadows. Keep interior detail minimal so the outlines stay readable.

options.what: Every line in the piece shares the same weight regardless of size or role.
options.looks: Consistent, systematic lines; objects of all sizes share one weight.
options.motion: Scaling does not change weight (non-scaling stroke); draw-ons feel mechanical and even.
options.use: Icon systems, infographics, UI-derived illustration, diagrams.
options.vs: Monoline is a whole-drawing style made of one continuous-weight line; uniform is a rule applied across all elements. Variable width varies.
options.prompt: Apply one stroke weight (e.g. 3px at 1080p) to every line in icons, diagrams, illustrations and borders, with vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke so zooms and scales never thicken or thin lines.

options.what: Lines that swell and taper along their length, like a brush or pen responding to pressure.
options.looks: Thick-to-thin strokes, tapered ends, calligraphic feel.
options.motion: Write-on reveals via masks (dashoffset alone cannot animate variable-width shapes), brush-like sweeps.
options.use: Premium illustration, lettering, fashion, calligraphic and cultural brands.
options.vs: Ink is variable width with a specific wet, liquid character; uniform never varies.
options.prompt: Draw lines as filled outlines that taper to points at both ends (2px to 8px to 2px at 1080p). Reveal them by animating a centerline mask path (a thick stroke used as SVG mask, stroke-dashoffset from length to 0) over 500-800ms.

options.what: Lines with jagged, textured or broken edges, like dry media or low-fi scans.
options.looks: Grainy edges, broken lines, charcoal or crayon texture, rough.js-style sketchiness.
options.motion: Jittery boil, stepped frame rates, texture flicker.
options.use: Indie brands, education, whiteboard styles, handmade aesthetics.
options.vs: Hand-drawn is about wobble and gesture; rough is about edge texture. Marker is smooth and saturated.
options.prompt: Render lines with rough edges: rough.js style sketch (roughness 1.2-1.8, bowing 1) or an SVG feTurbulence displacement (scale 2-3) on 3px strokes. Re-seed the roughness every 3 frames to boil.

options.what: Lines drawn visibly by hand: wobbly, overshooting, uneven.
options.looks: Wobbles, overshoots at corners, slight gaps, varying weight.
options.use: Explainers, annotations over UI, creative tools, education.
options.vs: Rough is edge texture; marker is a specific tool; hand-drawn is gesture and wobble.
options.prompt: Draw lines with deliberate wobble (2-4px deviation), overshooting corners by 4-8px, small gaps at joins, 3-4px average weight. Write on with stroke-dashoffset, then boil between 3 path variants every 3 frames.

options.what: A drawing style made of a single constant-weight line, often one continuous path.
options.looks: Even-weight line drawings, continuous-line illustrations, monoline lettering.
options.motion: One uninterrupted draw-on tracing the whole drawing, path morphs between drawings.
options.use: Minimal brand illustration, logo animations, elegant explainers.
options.vs: Uniform is a rule applied across a system of elements; monoline is the drawing style itself. Monoline icons are the icon-scale version.
options.prompt: Draw illustrations as one continuous 3px monoline path with round caps; animate the entire path drawing on in a single stroke-dashoffset tween (1.5-3s, ease power1.inOut), then morph the path into the next drawing.

options.what: Precise drafting-style lines: dimension lines, dashed hidden lines, construction lines.
options.looks: Thin 1-1.5px lines, dashed and dotted lines, arrows and dimension marks, blueprint or CAD feel.
options.motion: Precise draw-ons, measurement lines extending with numbers counting, dashed lines marching.
options.use: Hardware, engineering, developer tools, product exploded views.
options.vs: Hairline is only a weight; technical is a line vocabulary (dashes, dimensions, construction).
options.prompt: Use 1-1.5px lines with square caps; hidden edges dashed (stroke-dasharray 6 4), construction lines dotted at 40% opacity, dimension lines with 45-degree ticks and monospace numbers. Draw on in 300-500ms, ease power1.inOut; march dashes by animating dashoffset.

options.what: Lines imitating felt-tip or permanent marker: bold, saturated, slightly uneven.
options.looks: Thick rounded strokes, slight transparency overlaps, bleed, flat saturated color.
options.motion: Quick scribble reveals, highlighting strokes, circling and underlining.
options.use: Annotations, highlighting key UI, education, whiteboard explainers, youth brands.
options.vs: Ink has liquid variable width; hand-drawn is broader; marker is a specific bold felt-tip look.
options.prompt: Draw marker strokes at 8-14px (1080p) with round caps, 85-90% opacity so overlaps darken, slight edge roughness; use them to circle, underline and highlight. Scribble on fast: stroke-dashoffset over 250-400ms, ease power2.out.

options.what: Lines imitating brush pen or dip-pen ink: variable width, liquid, high contrast.
options.looks: Black liquid strokes with tapers, splatters, dry-brush breaks, sumi-e or comic-inking feel.
options.motion: Brush-reveal masks, ink spreading, splatter hits.
options.use: Cultural brands, editorial illustration, food, craft, dramatic title sequences.
options.vs: Variable width can be clean vector; ink carries wet texture and splatter. Marker is uniform and saturated.
options.prompt: Draw with black ink strokes: variable width 1-10px with sharp tapers, occasional dry-brush breaks and 2-3 small splatters. Reveal with a brush-shaped mask sweeping along the stroke direction (600-900ms, ease power2.out).

options.what: Parallel paired strokes tracing each form.
options.looks: Two thin lines with a gap (2-6px), inline or retro signage feel.
options.motion: Lines separate or merge, draw on in sequence, offset rhythm.
options.use: Retro and Art Deco styling, badges, signage-style graphics, luxury.
options.vs: Offset-line shifts a duplicate line out of registration; double-line keeps two parallel lines in precise registration.
options.prompt: Trace each form with two parallel 1.5px strokes separated by a 4px gap (a stroked outline plus an inset path). Draw the outer line first, the inner 120ms later, both via stroke-dashoffset over 500ms.

options.what: Outline and fill (or two line copies) deliberately shifted out of register.
options.looks: Fills offset 4-10px from their outlines, risograph and screen-print misregistration.
options.motion: Outline and fill sliding into or out of register, jittery misalignment.
options.use: Riso and print-inspired brands, editorial illustration, playful culture brands.
options.conveys: Handmade print charm, playfulness, analog warmth.
options.vs: Double-line keeps precise parallel registration; offset-line is intentionally misregistered.
options.prompt: Offset each shape's outline 6-8px down-right from its fill, outline 3px dark, fill in a riso-like color with multiply blending. Animate the offset from 0 to full on entry (300ms, ease power3.out) and jitter it 1-2px every 4 frames.

options.what: Lines reveal progressively along their paths as the core motion idea.
options.looks: Any line style; the line visibly travels from start to end.
options.motion: stroke-dashoffset animation, sequential path reveals, connectors drawing between elements.
options.use: Diagrams, logo reveals, illustration builds, signature and handwriting moments.
options.vs: A wipe reveal uncovers a static line with a moving mask edge; draw-on grows the line along its own path direction.
options.prompt: For each path set stroke-dasharray to its total length and animate stroke-dashoffset from length to 0 (DrawSVGPlugin '0%' to '100%' works too) over 400-900ms, ease power1.inOut; sequence paths in reading order with 60-120ms overlaps; fills fade in only after strokes finish.
